adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When the fallback branch runs, `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), which will almost always yield no match, making `selectedCalendar` undefined. This breaks the intended fallback-to-destination-calendar behavior and can cause updates to use the wrong calendar (or fail if downstream requires a calendarId).

adjudication_records.issue_text: In CalendarService.ts deleteEvent (~312-315), the same tautological fallback makes calendarId undefined when externalCalendarId isn't supplied, causing event deletion to silently fail and leaving orphaned Google Calendar events after cancellation

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `deleteEvent` (and similarly `updateEvent`), the fallback calendar selection is incorrect: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is not supplied (undefined/null), the `find` predicate becomes `cal.externalId === undefined`, which will almost always return `undefined`, so `calendarId` is not derived from `event.destinationCalendar` as intended. This is a real logic bug introduced by the diff and can prevent deleting/updating events on the correct calendar when no `externalCalendarId` is provided.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts (Google) updateEvent/deleteEvent contains a dead fallback: the else branch is only reached when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate cal.externalId === externalCalendarId can never match, leaving calendarId undefined and making events un-updatable/un-cancellable for affected bookings

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the only time the else branch runs), the `.find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, so it will not match normal calendars and will typically return `undefined`. That leaves `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` undefined, which can break updates/deletes for bookings that rely on destinationCalendar rather than an explicit `externalCalendarId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Collective multiple-hosts support is only implemented for Google Calendar; Lark, Office365, and CalDav services take only the first element of destinationCalendar, so secondary hosts silently receive no events while the booking record shows success

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, appends other hosts’ `destinationCalendar`s (`handleNewBooking.ts`: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` then iterates over each destination and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, expecting per-destination creation. However, non-Google calendar services still effectively use only the first destination calendar: Lark (`LarkCalendarService.createEvent/createAttendees/updateEvent/deleteEvent`) destructures `[mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and uses that externalId; Office365 does the same in `createEvent`; CalDAV/BaseCalendarService filters by only the first destination calendar’s externalId. Only Google’s `createEvent` was updated to select the calendar by `credentialId` from the destinationCalendar array. This means when creating events for secondary hosts (non-first destinations) on Lark/Office365/CalDAV, the service will target the first host’s calendar (or error), so secondary hosts won’t reliably get events despite multi-destination iteration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:497 updateAllCalendarEvents merge path uses .find for old calendar references, so reschedule/merge deletes only the first calendar reference and orphans old events on secondary hosts' calendars

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents, calendar references were changed from a single ref to an array via `.filter(...)` and the code now loops `for (const reference of calendarReference) { ... }`. However, in the merge path (`if (newBookingId) { ... }`) it still does `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));`, i.e., only the first calendar reference is considered for deletion. If there are multiple `_calendar` references (e.g., secondary hosts/destination calendars), only one old event will be deleted and the others can be orphaned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking.ts:447 recurring-cancel path still uses .find to look up calendar references, deleting only one calendar event per booking and leaving stale events on secondary hosts' calendars when cancelling a recurring collective booking

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts, although the top-level cancellation flow was updated to use `filter` and iterate over all `_calendar` references (`bookingToDelete.references.filter(...)` and `for (const reference ...)`), the recurring-cancel branch still does `const bookingRef = updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"));` when deleting events for `updatedBookings`. With destination calendars now supporting multiple calendars/hosts (array), a booking can have multiple `_calendar` references; using `.find` deletes only the first reference per updated booking, leaving other calendar events stale on secondary hosts' calendars.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new multi-destination/multi-host calendar behavior (e.g., `destinationCalendar` changes from single to array; `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` and may fetch credentials from DB; `updateBooking` now processes *all* `_calendar` references via `filter(...)` and loops; `handleCancelBooking` now deletes events for all `_calendar` references). However, the only test change in the diff is in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts`, updating an expectation from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []`. There are no added/updated tests asserting the new collective multi-host semantics (one event per host calendar, multiple references, multi-calendar updates/deletes), so the finding is a specific, diff-grounded gap in test coverage rather than a directly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventResult.externalId is the destination calendar's id rather than the created event's id, and is only populated in one of two creation branches: the no-credentialId branch calls createEvent without the third argument, leaving references without a calendar id and breaking later updates/deletes

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `CalendarManager.createEvent(...)` now returns `EventResult` with `externalId` taken from its new third argument (see `return { ..., externalId, credentialId: credential.id }`). In `EventManager` where booking references are built, `externalCalendarId` is now set from `result.externalId` (e.g. `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined`). However, in `createAllCalendarEvents`, the branch where `destination.credentialId` is missing calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing that third argument, so `result.externalId` (and thus stored `externalCalendarId`) will be `undefined` even if `event.destinationCalendar` contains an `externalId`. That can lead to later update/delete using the wrong calendar (often falling back to primary) because the reference lacks the external calendar id. The finding’s claim that `externalId` should be the created event’s id is not supported by the diff (it is used as the calendar id), but the “only populated in one branch leading to missing externalCalendarId in references” part is a real defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:256 (updateEvent) and :315 (deleteEvent) — dead fallback branch: the .find() predicate cal.externalId === externalCalendarId never matches because find only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so selectedCalendar/calendarId is always undefined, causing updates/deletes without externalCalendarId to send calendarId: undefined and never update or delete stale calendar events

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, updateEvent and deleteEvent now compute the calendar id as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. The `.find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but the predicate compares `cal.externalId` to that same falsy `externalCalendarId` (undefined/null), so it will almost always return undefined. This makes the fallback logic effectively dead and can lead to using an undefined/incorrect calendarId when no externalCalendarId is provided, breaking updates/deletes for events stored on a non-primary destination calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:117-119 — dropped optional chaining: dereferencing .integration on the destructured mainHostDestinationCalendar crashes with TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or an empty array (a [] value this diff now produces in requestReschedule.handler.ts and handleNewBooking.ts), breaking event creation for Google Meet bookings with no destination calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the diff introduces `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then checks `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`, destructuring yields `undefined`, so accessing `.integration` will throw a `TypeError`. adjudication_records.issue_text: organizations/create.handler.ts:150-153 — condition inverted relative to old code: slug is now set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true instead of when billing is disabled, so with billing disabled organizations are created with no slug at all (previously they got one immediately), silently flipping slug/requestedSlug semantics

adjudication.rationale: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts the spread conditions were flipped: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, and similarly `requestedSlug` is now only set when billing is enabled. From the diff alone, when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, neither `slug` nor `metadata.requestedSlug` is set at all, whereas previously a slug was set immediately. That is a concrete behavior change consistent with the finding (organizations created with billing disabled will now have no slug).

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarManager.ts:266-267 and EventManager.ts:169 — externalId in the result is the echoed input argument rather than the calendar the event actually landed in; GoogleCalendarService.ts:152 can fall back to the 'primary' calendar while the booking reference records destination.externalId (or undefined), causing reschedules and cancellations to target the wrong calendar and produce 404s/orphaned events

adjudication.rationale: In `CalendarManager.createEvent`, the returned `EventResult` now includes `externalId` that is just the echoed input argument (`externalId` param passed from `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` via `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`), not the calendar actually used by the calendar integration. In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the insert `calendarId` is computed as `selectedCalendar || "primary"` where `selectedCalendar` is derived by matching `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar` against the *credentialId*; if no match exists, the event is created in `primary`. That means the operation can succeed in `primary` while `result.externalId` still reflects the requested destination externalId (or undefined), and `EventManager` persists `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` into booking references. Subsequent update/delete paths use that stored `externalCalendarId`, which can target the wrong calendar and cause 404s/orphaned events. This mismatch is directly shown by the diff wiring and the fallback-to-primary behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the only change in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts` is `destinationCalendar: null` → `destinationCalendar: []` (a shape update consistent with `destinationCalendar` becoming an array throughout the PR). There are no added assertions or new scenarios in that e2e diff that would exercise the newly added multi-destination fan-out in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` (now loops `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)`), nor the new credentialId-based selection in Google `createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)` (selects calendar via `.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`). So the finding that the test update is cosmetic and doesn’t validate the headline new behavior is supported by the diff; it plausibly wouldn’t catch regressions like only using the first destination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: office365calendar/CalendarService.ts:73-76 and larkcalendar/CalendarService.ts:128 — non-Google services ignore the passed destination externalId and always read destinationCalendar[0] (the organizer's), so in mixed-provider collective bookings the Office365/Lark service constructs URLs using the Google host's externalId, causing 404/wrong-calendar creation for non-first hosts

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over all destination calendars/credentials to create multiple events. GoogleCalendarService was updated to pick the destination calendar matching the current `credentialId` (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), but Office365 and Lark services were changed to always destructure the first entry (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];`) and use its `externalId` when building the API URL / calendarId. In collective/multi-host scenarios where `evt.destinationCalendar` contains multiple calendars (organizer first, then other hosts appended), this will cause non-first hosts’ Office365/Lark event creation to use the organizer/first host’s externalId, leading to wrong-calendar operations or 404s.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:1874-1879 only persists the first host's destinationCalendar via connect on evt.destinationCalendar[0], silently dropping the rest and leaving cancellation/reschedule paths unable to update or delete events on hosts 2..N's calendars

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `handleNewBooking.ts` builds `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array and, for collective team events, appends additional team members’ destination calendars (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, when persisting the booking it only connects `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` (the first calendar) to the DB (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`), so any additional destination calendars are not persisted via the `destinationCalendar` relation. That said, the claim that this makes cancellation/reschedule unable to update/delete events for hosts 2..N is not verifiable from the diff, because the cancellation/update/delete paths were refactored to operate over *calendar references* (`references.filter(type.includes('_calendar'))`) and iterate them, which should still allow per-host calendar operations without relying on `booking.destinationCalendar`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:253-254 and :312-313 (Google) has a dead-code fallback where find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) searches for a falsy externalId and always returns undefined, making update/delete target calendarId: undefined instead of the destination calendar, orphaning events for legacy bookings

adjudication.rationale:
In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback branch when externalCalendarId is falsy is:

- updateEvent: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`
- deleteEvent: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`

But in that branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined/""), so the `.find(...)` predicate searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is falsy, which will almost always return `undefined` instead of selecting a destination calendar from `event.destinationCalendar`. This makes the fallback effectively dead and can cause update/delete to target no specific destination calendar (falling back elsewhere, e.g., to "primary" or an invalid/undefined calendarId depending on the call site), which can break legacy bookings that lack an externalCalendarId reference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarManager.ts:227-267 returns the requested externalId in the EventResult rather than the calendar actually written to, so the stored BookingReference can point at a calendar where the event does not exist (e.g., primary fallback in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent, or the .catch path storing externalCalendarId for an event that was never created)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts`, `createEvent(...)` now returns an `EventResult` that includes `externalId` taken directly from the function argument (added at lines ~217-267) rather than deriving it from what calendar the integration actually wrote to. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts#createEvent`, the code can fall back to inserting into `"primary"` when no matching destination calendar is found (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`), but `CalendarManager` will still report the requested `externalId` passed in from `EventManager#createAllCalendarEvents` (`createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`). Additionally, even when `createEvent` fails (the `.catch` sets `success = false` and returns `undefined`), `CalendarManager` still returns an `EventResult` object containing that `externalId`, which `EventManager` then uses as `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` when building booking references. This can cause stored references to point at a calendar where the event was not created / does not exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:337-380 writes multiple BookingReference rows with the same type (e.g., two google_calendar references) per booking without any Prisma schema change or migration, risking a unique-constraint violation on @@unique([bookingId, type]) that breaks booking creation mid-deploy and orphans provider events

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now iterates over an array of destinationCalendar entries and may create multiple calendar events (and other code switches from find() to filter() for *_calendar references), but this diff does not show any code that actually *writes* BookingReference rows, nor does it include (or prove the existence of) a Prisma @@unique([bookingId, type]) constraint. The finding’s claim of a guaranteed unique-constraint violation and orphaned provider events depends on schema details not present in the diff, so it isn’t verifiable from what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lark CalendarService.ts:127-128 always uses element [0] of destinationCalendar regardless of which host credential is being invoked, creating every Lark event for a multi-host collective booking on the first host's calendar and none on the others (similar pattern in office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73-76)

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: LarkCalendarService.createEvent now derives calendarId from `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;` (and similarly in createAttendees/updateEvent/deleteEvent), so it always targets destinationCalendar[0]. Meanwhile, for collective/team events the diff explicitly builds a multi-entry `evt.destinationCalendar` array (`handleNewBooking.ts`: collects `teamDestinationCalendars` and then `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`), and EventManager now loops `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` to create events per destination/credential. Because Lark (and Office365) ignore which destination/credential is being invoked and always use index 0, multi-host collective bookings would create all Lark/Office365 events on the first host's calendar and not on others.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:984-1000 populates teamDestinationCalendars via side-effect pushes inside an async map with no ordering guarantee, making the destination list and which host's calendar is persisted as [0] nondeterministic/fragile

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the `teamDestinationCalendars.push(...)` occurs before the first `await` (`getTranslation(...)`) inside the `async` map callback, so those pushes execute synchronously in the deterministic order of `users.slice(1)` during the `map` call. Also, the persisted calendar reference uses `evt.destinationCalendar[0]`, which is set earlier from `eventType.destinationCalendar` or `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` (not from `teamDestinationCalendars`). If `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, the later `?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op, so team calendars wouldn't become `[0]` anyway. Thus the claimed nondeterminism / fragile selection of `[0]` is not supported by the diff.
